name: Lords Chloro Alkali Ltd
title: Lords Chloro Alkali Ltd - 500284 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Caustic soda volumes up 29.7% to 84,690 t in FY26 with EBITDA margin 16.89%, but Q4 margin slipped to 14.03% on grid power repricing; capacity expansion to 360 TPD is on track, with 80–85% utilisation and no North India capacity additions announced.

summary.headline: FY26 PAT rose 360.9% to INR28.49 crore on caustic soda volume up 29.7% to 84,690 MT; Q4 EBITDA margin 14.03% hit by grid power tariff revision.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 as a step-up year: total income INR393.1 crore (+44.62% YoY), EBITDA INR66.38 crore (+159%) at a 16.89% margin (+747 bps). Q4 FY26 total income was INR97.75 crore (+22.3% YoY), EBITDA INR13.72 crore at 14.03% margin (up 247 bps QoQ), and PAT INR4.39 crore (+68.64% YoY). Q4 margins were below Q3's stated level of above 20% because the grid power rate revision effective 1 October 2025 persisted and one electrolyser was shut for renovation, raising power consumption. Management said a 21 MW solar plant in Rajasthan is due around mid-June 2026, with renewables expected to rise to 40-45% of power needs.

financial_highlights.change: +247 bps QoQ; YoY bps change not quantified
from INR181.67 crore a year ago

financial_highlights.value: approx. 0.67x; long-term debt INR96.37 crore, short-term INR65.58 crore

segments.name: Caustic soda lye
segments.commentary: FY26 volume 84,690 MT (+29.7%) and Q4 volume 20,935 MT (+8.72% YoY). Management said realisations improved QoQ and prices remain about 12-15% above pre-war levels after a March spike of 30-35%.

segments.name: Chlorinated paraffin wax (CPW)
segments.commentary: Contributed meaningfully to Q4 revenue. Capacity is being expanded from 50 to 100 TPD, and management cited it as converting chlorine into a value-added product that stabilises the mix.

guidance_outlook: 21 MW solar plant in Rajasthan expected to be commissioned around mid-June 2026; renewable share expected to rise from about 15-20% to 40-45% of power needs.

10 MW hybrid wind-solar group captive project: management said full 100 MW wind component to be completed next month and full contracted units expected from June 2026 onward, after the shortfall (about 97 lakh units) that was credited to power expenses under the agreement.
Expects caustic capacity utilisation of 80-85% over the next year.
Total installed capacity to reach 360 TPD after the 100 TPD caustic expansion, with an old 40 TPD plant decommissioned (gross would have been 400 TPD).
Management expects the energy-cost benefit to ease margin pressure once renewables are running; expects Q4's power-cost headwind to recede.
Plans to raise about INR90 crore of additional long-term debt; cost of debt around 8% (total about 7.9%).
capex_capacity: Total capex outlay INR315 crore over FY24 to FY27-28; first phase of INR150 crore (90 TPD caustic expansion, 16 MW Bikaner solar, equity in 10 MW hybrid project) completed.
Second phase under execution: 21 MW captive solar, CPW expansion from 50 to 100 TPD, and a further 100 TPD caustic soda expansion. Capital WIP INR43.85 crore at year-end.
Caustic soda capacity to reach 360 TPD post-expansion; new caustic capacity comes online around end-FY27, per analyst's reading of management's timeline.
Sulfuric acid project deferred due to volatile global sulfur prices; management cited heat-recovery use for a planned flaking unit as the rationale.
demand_pricing: Management cited India caustic demand growth of about 5-6% nationally and 4-5% in North India; no new North India capacity is announced in the next 15-18 months, and management sees none for 2-2.5 years. Company has 300 TPD of a roughly 1,600 TPD North India capacity (about 20%), rising to 26-27% after expansion.
Management said salt is contracted yearly at about 11-12% of production cost, with consumption of 1.61-1.62 t salt per t caustic; purification chemicals rose 20-30% but are only 1-2% of cost.
Caustic soda prices spiked 30-35% in March 2026 and have since eased to about 12-15% above pre-war levels, per management.

Management said Indian capacity additions of 2-2.5 million tonnes over three years are largely captive for PVC on the West Coast and expected to export; chlorine prices are currently negative in India.

qa_highlights.question: Shortfall of about 97 lakh units from the consortium: how is it accounted and will it reverse?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the shortfall reflected committed units not supplied under the power purchase agreement, that the credit taken in power expenses is not reversible, and that full units are expected from June 2026 as the wind project completes.

qa_highlights.question: With utilisation near 80% and new capacity only at end-FY27, how will quarterly growth come?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said utilisation should reach 80-85% over the next year, with demand exceeding North India supply given no new regional capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the sulfuric acid plant deferred?
qa_highlights.answer: Sulfur supply has been volatile for six to nine months and the war began about three months ago, so the project is on the back burner pending stability.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 margin fall versus Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Grid tariff revision applied in both quarters; caustic prices eased QoQ, and an electrolyser shutdown for membrane and electrode renovation raised power consumption in the last months of the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What are the net renewable savings and power cost without solar?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a figure. It said the grid landed cost rose from about INR7 to INR8.2-8.3 per unit (a 15-18% rise) and that renewables are about 15-20% of power today.

qa_highlights.question: Cost of debt and FY27 interest outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Average cost of debt is a little under 8% (about 7.9%) and INR90 crore of additional long-term debt is planned.

qa_highlights.question: Is further renewable capex planned beyond current projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is evaluating more opportunities, pausing until the 21 MW project is done and domestic cell mandates settle, with a stated aim of maximising renewable share within regulations.

qa_highlights.question: Will new South and West Coast capacity cause oversupply in the domestic market?
qa_highlights.answer: Management argued that new capacity is PVC-linked and export-oriented, that chlorine-caustic (ECU) pricing offsets, and that the North India market is small and fragmented.

risks_watch: Q4 margin of 14.03% versus Q3's above 20%: whether electrolyser renovation and the grid tariff of about INR8.2-8.3/unit are reversed in Q1 FY27.
Realisations: prices are still 12-15% above pre-war levels and could fall further as the market normalises.
Capacity timing: 21 MW solar and 100 TPD caustic/CPW expansions are due around mid-June 2026 and end-FY27; delays would hit volume and margin guidance.
Sulfur and sulfuric acid supply volatility, plus deferral of the acid project.
Debt rising by about INR90 crore at around 8% cost, with capex of INR315 crore funded by accruals and debt.
Future new capacity from West Coast PVC-linked players could affect pricing, though management argues it is export-oriented.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY26 growth and the renewable cost story, but cautious on near-term timing (solar commissioning, wind units, sulfuric acid). Several answers were vague on specifics, including the renewable savings figure and the reconciliation of the 97 lakh-unit shortfall.
key_quotes: I am pleased to report that the financial year 2026 has been a landmark year for Lords Chloro Alkali Limited.
We expect this headwind to ease meaningfully once our 21 megawatt solar plant in Rajasthan is commissioned around mid-June '26.
Financial year 2026 marks an inflection point for Lords Chloro Alkali.
So, this year we should see the full number of units which we were to get, getting from June onwards.

growth.why: Management guides caustic utilisation of 80-85% over the next year and post-expansion capacity of 360 TPD (100 TPD expansion, likely around end-FY27 per analyst reading), backed by capex under execution and a 21 MW solar plant due mid-June 2026, but no revenue growth figure is guided and there are no firm orders cited.
